reviewedInvariants.result: One private static actor accepts all instances and all four asynchronous operation kinds. Its submit body has no await; each detached job explicitly awaits its captured predecessor tail before synchronous I/O. Order is actual admission, independent of actor FIFO or caller Task construction. onSubmit is a bounded synchronous observation, not a guarantee that a worker has not already started.

Atomic persistence, onSave and success logging execute within the same ordered job. A thrown file failure logs without onSave and normally resolves the nonthrowing job, allowing later jobs. An admitted detached job completes its success/failure handling even if the caller is cancelled.

Async load runs unchanged read/decode in the detached worker. The admitted no-op flush awaits the same chain and is a real completion barrier for admitted predecessors. loadSync remains direct synchronous caller I/O with no wait on pending jobs.

Default sync replacement and owned-root helper share the same worker. A batch is one ordered operation, catches per-file failures, traces main state/count, and deliberately omits onSave to preserve Firestore pull without push echo.
Exactly one existing production caller changes solely by awaiting replacement completion.
Byte comparison proves the sole model change is Sendable; stored Int/optional Int values and Codable JSON remain unchanged.

Function-body comparison proves unchanged loadSync and writePosition. Atomic writes and per-write directory creation remain. No new GCD queue, storage index/cache, main synchronous worker wait or try? was added.
Tests/iOS remains the synchronized root for yuedu appTests with no test-source exclusion. The new file extends the existing @MainActor XCTest class without requiring project per-file references.

testReview.coverage: Owned real files and held writes cover cancellation, cross-instance order, async read/flush barriers, failed atomic write followed by success, directory removal/recreation, cold store reopen and sync-import no echo. Readiness uses recorded admission, writer entry and completion signals. Five-second waits are failure deadlines; no settle sleeps/yields are used.
testReview.cleanup: Cleanup opens the gate, cancels caller wrappers and waits at most five seconds for real completion. Every signal supplies a fresh expectation, and the owned directory is retained on failed drain.

resolvedFinding.issue: A nonfatal main assertion followed by NSCondition.wait would block the MainActor under the exact off-main regression being tested.
resolvedFinding.resolution: The fixture now fails and throws unexpectedMainThread before the blocking gate if called on main.

toolingReview.inventory: 10 persistence/order methods/executions + 3 scroll methods/12 executions + 5 migration methods/6 executions.

The portable gate test rejects stale 13/23, mixed 13/28 and 18/23, 27/29 execution counts, missing/duplicate devices, bool counts, failures/skips/expected failures.

grammarRecord.meaning: Tree-sitter grammar screen only; not Swift typecheck.

boundaries: Order starts at actual actor admission; concurrent Task creation or wall-clock calls are not FIFO contracts.
Flush is a process-local barrier for admitted predecessors, including other books/stores. No crash durability, fsync or multi-file atomicity is established.

Existing files under the default atomic writer yield old or new complete loadSync snapshots without waiting. Missing, deleted or corrupt files preserve the previous nil/log behavior. loadSync itself still performs synchronous I/O on its caller.
Default onSave still schedules an independent MainActor Task: ordered worker callbacks do not establish FIFO of later cloud scheduling, debounce or network pushes.
Remote fetch staleness, merge conflict policy and external/process writes are outside this batch.
The admission observer must remain short and nonblocking. Production defaults to no-op; owned test observation records locked snapshots and fulfills signals.
The shared chain serializes all stores/books. Throughput, latency and physical-device smoothness have not been measured.
Static checks and portable tests do not prove Swift type correctness, Apple SDK compilation, XCTest runtime success or hardware storage/background behavior.
